fragments.text: Target edition: 17 October 2026. Easel is connected FP&A for small and mid-size finance teams. A US finance lead or fractional CFO buys it instead of Workday Adaptive Planning, Planful or Anaplan, and it has to beat what Runway, Pigment and Aleph offer the same buyer. It provides flexible driver models; rolling profit-and-loss, balance-sheet and cash forecasts; headcount and compensation planning; scenarios; and board reporting. All of it is fed live from the ledger, payroll and the CRM, with every number traceable to its source and every approval kept as an immutable record.

This contract describes the product Easel is being built towards, not only what exists today. The [Status](#status) table shows how close the current code is. The 17 published clauses (`EASEL-001` to `EASEL-017`) are the shipped monthly planning loop. The target clauses complete the category job, and the push-further clauses take agents beyond today's up-and-comers. Difficulty (provider OAuth apps, Office add-ins, payroll and CRM connectors, native apps) is engineering work recorded as a clause. It is never a reason to drop scope.
| Category | FP&A (financial planning and analysis) software |
| Incumbents a buyer switches from | Workday Adaptive Planning, Planful, Anaplan, Runway, Pigment, Aleph |

| First buyer | A US finance lead or fractional CFO at a business with 25 to 250 employees, closing its books in QuickBooks Online, Xero, NetSuite or Sage Intacct, paying people through Gusto, Rippling or a PEO such as Justworks or TriNet, budgeting with department heads who enter their own numbers each autumn, selling through HubSpot or Salesforce, and planning in USD |

For that buyer, switching means that their ledger (with its history), payroll roster, pipeline and subscription data arrive through live connectors or mapped files; their budget owners enter numbers in a planning grid as they did in the incumbent's sheets; their Excel or Google Sheets model arrives with its formulas; every planning job they ran in the incumbent (budget, rolling forecast, headcount, scenarios, department submissions, board pack, cash alerts) has an Easel equivalent; and their old tool's versions are imported with a list of what did not map.
A buyer replacing an incumbent needs the whole job, so the target is the whole job:

**Connected actuals.** QuickBooks Online, Xero, NetSuite, Sage Intacct and [Pantry](https://github.com/just-every/run-pantry) actuals backfill up to 36 months of history on first connection and refresh on a schedule, with reusable account, department and class mapping, balance-sheet balances, freshness and drill-through to the ledger transaction (`CONNECT-*`, `EASEL-002` to `EASEL-004`).

**A flexible model.** A planning grid with paste, spreading, copy forward, split sub-rows and cell notes; plans built from prior-year actuals; user-defined formulas, dimensions and hierarchies, a configurable rolling horizon, multi-year plans and starter models for subscription, services and project businesses (`MODEL-*`, `EASEL-006`, `EASEL-008`).

**Three statements and cash.** A linked P&L, balance sheet and cash-flow forecast with receivables and payables timing, deferred revenue, debt, capex and depreciation, runway, a 13-week cash view and US tax estimates (`FIN-*`, `EASEL-005`).

**Headcount and compensation.** A roster from Gusto, Rippling or [Willow](https://github.com/just-every/run-willow), or a mapped roster and payroll-register file from any PEO or payroll provider, open roles from [Lodge](https://github.com/just-every/run-lodge) or Greenhouse, and US compensation assumptions (W-2 and 1099, employer payroll taxes with wage bases, benefits, bonus, commission), with salary visible only to those allowed (`PEOPLE-*`, `EASEL-007`).

**Revenue and pipeline.** Pipeline from [Orbit](https://github.com/just-every/run-orbit), HubSpot and Salesforce with explicit probability and timing assumptions, and subscription metrics (ARR, churn, cohorts) from Stripe Billing or [Nectar](https://github.com/just-every/run-nectar) (`REV-*`).
**Spreadsheets kept live.** Two-way Excel and Google Sheets add-ins whose formulas stay live, model import that keeps formulas, and Excel exports with formulas (`SHEET-*`, `EASEL-015`).

**Planning cycles.** Budget calendars, tasks, reminders and escalations, metric-triggered tasks, quarterly reforecasts, long-range plans, private and shared scenarios, per-department ordered approval chains, groups and per-dimension permissions (`CYCLE-*`, `EASEL-009` to `EASEL-012`).
**Reporting.** A report builder, dashboards, board packs in PDF, PowerPoint and Excel, scheduled cash alerts, and BI and warehouse feeds (`REPORT-*`, `EASEL-013`, `EASEL-014`).

**Move in and out.** Imports from Adaptive Planning, Planful, Anaplan, Runway and Pigment exports, a parallel month against the old tool, and complete exports and restores (`MOVE-*`, `PORT-*`, `EASEL-016`).

**Anywhere and governed.** Phone-width review and approvals, native iOS and Android apps with push, SSO and SCIM, an audit trail, person erasure, multi-entity and multi-currency plans, a public API, webhooks and an MCP endpoint (`MOBILE-*`, `ACCESS-*`, `AUDIT-*`, `ERASE-*`, `ENTITY-*`, `API-*`).

**Agents that keep the plan feasible.** They watch actuals, pipeline and hiring, flag when a change breaks an agreed cash or runway constraint, compute feasible responses for the owner to choose, chase uncertain assumptions, and learn from the company's own forecast errors (`AGENT-*`).

Easel is one product. Where the market sells a neighboring product separately, Easel connects to it and does not rebuild it. When the neighbor is a Run Edit Run sibling, Easel connects to that sibling first and to the US incumbent second.

**Target clauses** are the `#### ID — Title.` headings in [Target clauses](#target-clauses), and **push-further clauses** are the ones in [Push further](#push-further). They are binding product requirements that are not yet registered. A build round that starts one registers it in `seed.json → capabilities` in the same change and adds its flow test. IDs never change.

**Status** is `done`, `partial` or `missing`, judged from the code and tests at the commit named in [Status](#status). `done` means the behavior ships and a cited test or journey exercises it. `partial` means some of it ships, or there is code with no test that exercises the behavior. `missing` means there is no implementation. Status is a build-planning judgment, not acceptance. [ACCEPTANCE.md](ACCEPTANCE.md) decides acceptance.

**Acceptance runs through public doors**: the HTTP API (`API.md`), the browser at 1440 and 390 pixels, `rer` commands, an Office or Google add-in, a native app, or an import or export file. Fakes are allowed only at a paid or network edge (a provider API, a model API, a mail or chat relay). A provider fake proves Easel's semantics, never live provider behavior, so a connector clause also needs one recorded run against the provider's sandbox before it is accepted.

These are the guarantees of the shipped monthly planning loop for one company. It uses uploaded files, local storage and a reporting currency chosen at setup, and needs no provider account. Posted accounting truth stays in the accounting system. Easel holds assumptions, estimates, alternatives, approvals and the review record. The target clauses below extend each of these into the connected product; none of them is withdrawn.

**EASEL-001 — Setup, roles and membership.** Finance (the claimed owner and any Base admin) sets the company name, reporting currency, fiscal-year start and first plan month (twelve months), departments (shared or not), planning lines (revenue, cost of sales, operating expense; payroll or not) and people.
Contributors are scoped to named departments; viewers read.
A signed-in person without an active Easel membership sees no plan data.
*Acceptance:* `tests/easel.test.mjs` `EASEL-001` and the planning journey in `tests/browser.mjs`.

**EASEL-002 — Actuals preview that writes nothing.** An actuals CSV preview reads the file with the person's column, sign and date choices and shows months covered, per-account totals with a sign check, department totals, and every rejected row with its line number and reason (malformed date or amount, missing account, both debit and credit, an exact repeat of an earlier line, a row already accepted in another import).
The preview writes nothing.
*Acceptance:* `tests/easel.test.mjs` `EASEL-002`.

**EASEL-003 — Mapped, reconciled actuals acceptance.** An actuals file is accepted only when every account maps to a planning line, the cash balance or an explicit exclusion, every department maps, the reviewed preview fingerprint still matches, and finance confirms the rejected rows stay out.
Acceptance goes through the Base import-kit journal with the exact original bytes.
Reconciliation shows, month by month, that imported = mapped + excluded + cash + unmapped, with unmapped accounts listed.
*Acceptance:* `tests/easel.test.mjs` `EASEL-003` and `tests/review-fixes.test.mjs`.
**EASEL-004 — Exact undo of an actuals import.** Undo of an accepted actuals import removes exactly the rows it wrote, through the journal.
An import whose months a forecast has already closed cannot be undone; a correcting file is imported instead.
*Acceptance:* `tests/easel.test.mjs` `EASEL-004`.

**EASEL-005 — Labeled opening cash and explicit cash timing.** Each scenario's opening cash is either an estimate the person enters or the balance imported from accepted rows mapped to the cash balance before the first plan month, and every cash figure says which.
Collections and payments follow explicit lags (months) plus opening receivables and payables; payroll is paid in its month.
Each month's cash shows its arithmetic.
*Acceptance:* `tests/easel.test.mjs` `EASEL-005`.

**EASEL-006 — Exact revenue drivers with traces.** Revenue comes from volume × rate (with monthly growth) or customers × revenue per customer (with churn, new customers per month and new customers per hire in a named department, ramped by the recorded ramp rule).
Every cell carries the arithmetic that produced it.
Money is integer cents, counts are hundredths and every division rounds half away from zero once; the same inputs always produce the same cells.
*Acceptance:* `tests/easel.test.mjs` `EASEL-006` and `tests/totals.test.mjs`.
**EASEL-007 — Position costs and restricted pay detail.** Positions (named or to be hired) cost annual salary ÷ 12 × (1 + owner-supplied on-costs) from start to end month.
Individual positions and salaries require the owner-granted Pay detail permission (`PEOPLE-005`); that grant lets finance see all departments and contributors only their own.

The sources behind another department's numbers remain restricted to finance and that department's contributors; viewers and other departments receive amounts with the detail removed by the server, and cannot change another department's inputs through any route.
*Acceptance:* `tests/easel.test.mjs` `EASEL-007`.
**EASEL-008 — Expenses, schedules and visible allocations.** Recurring and one-off expenses and imported monthly schedules feed their line and department.
A shared department's costs are allocated to other departments by monthly headcount or fixed shares adding to exactly 100%; line totals never change and every allocated amount names its rule.
Self, chained or unshared allocations, unknown lines or departments, and deleting a department or line still in use are refused.
*Acceptance:* `tests/easel.test.mjs` `EASEL-008` and `tests/totals.test.mjs`.
**EASEL-009 — Department submissions.** Finance requests submissions from departments.

A contributor revises only their own department's budget inputs while its submission is requested or returned, comments on their own department, and submits; a submitted department is locked until finance returns it with a reason.
The full request/submit/return history is kept.
*Acceptance:* `tests/easel.test.mjs` `EASEL-009` and `tests/review-fixes.test.mjs`.
**EASEL-010 — Exact-revision budget approval.** Finance approves the budget only at the exact revision reviewed and only when every requested department has submitted.
Approval freezes the budget and stores an immutable snapshot (inputs, outputs, approver, time, revision, submissions, SHA-256) that the database refuses to change or delete.
The forecast opens from the approved budget.
*Acceptance:* `tests/easel.test.mjs` `EASEL-010`.

**EASEL-011 — Scenario branch and comparison.** Finance branches any plan into a scenario (for example a downside with later hiring or higher churn) and compares two scenarios: monthly profit and closing cash side by side, every changed assumption, and every cell that moved.
*Acceptance:* `tests/easel.test.mjs` `EASEL-011`.
**EASEL-012 — Proposals promoted at exact revisions.** A proposal is a copy of a working plan bound to that plan's exact revision.

Its author (a contributor for their own departments, finance for any) changes it and submits it; finance promotes only the exact proposal revision reviewed, and only while the target is still at the bound revision.
Otherwise nothing changes.
Promotion records the target's revision before and after.
*Acceptance:* `tests/easel.test.mjs` `EASEL-012`.
**EASEL-013 — Month close and source-backed variance.** Finance closes the next month on the forecast once accepted actuals cover it.
The forecast as it stood is kept as an immutable snapshot first; closed months then use actuals.

For a closed month, each line and department shows actual against the approved budget and the kept forecast, with the accepted rows behind it, the budget sources, and a draft that marks any timing explanation as an unconfirmed hypothesis.
Finance or the department's contributor writes and confirms the business explanation.
*Acceptance:* `tests/easel.test.mjs` `EASEL-013` and the review journey at 390 in `tests/browser.mjs`.

**EASEL-014 — Published review pack with decisions.** Finance creates a review pack for a closed month, records decisions and actions, and publishes it as an immutable snapshot binding the numbers, the approved budget and forecast revisions, the accepted source files with their digests, the explanations and the decisions.
Every member, viewers included, can download it as HTML or CSV; it carries no individual pay detail.
Action progress is recorded without changing the pack.
*Acceptance:* `tests/easel.test.mjs` `EASEL-014`.

**EASEL-015 — Excel workbook move-in with provenance.** The Excel planning workbook kit reads an .xlsx sheet with Line, Department and month columns, uses each cell's cached value, keeps sheet, row, cell address and formula text as provenance, rounds to cents visibly, skips total rows, and requires every line and department to match or be mapped.
It stages the workbook as a new scenario through the import journal; undo removes what it wrote and keeps any row a person has since edited (and what that row needs).
*Acceptance:* `tests/easel.test.mjs` `EASEL-015` and `tests/workbook-undo.test.mjs`.

**EASEL-016 — Complete export and clean restore.** `rer export` writes the complete installation (model, actuals, journal and originals, approvals, kept forecasts, packs and activity); `rer import` refuses a non-empty destination or a corrupt archive and restores into a clean installation of the release that made it, which then shows the same model, approvals, outputs and packs and re-exports identical rows.
*Acceptance:* the export and restore steps of `tests/browser.mjs` and `tests/review-fixes.test.mjs`.

**EASEL-017 — Owned runtime on Base.** MIT source starts with one line, `npx -y @runeditrun/rer dev just-every/run-easel`, and the checkout runs through `rer` install, setup, dev, build, preview, verify, reset, export, import, deploy --dry-run, describe and check, on TanStack Start, Hono and Cloudflare D1, with self-hosted IBM Plex Sans, Easel's theme on Base's installer and sign-in pages, and dev identity with finance, sales, engineering and board personas.
Builds refuse the local dev layer.
*Acceptance:* `tests/browser.mjs`, `rer verify` and the GitHub Verify workflow.
The package-mode upgrade starts from the installed data and migrations of the earlier Easel application, before package mode.
Migrations `0001` through `0007` retain their original bytes; subsequent numbered migrations extend that schema.
The executed in-place upgrade retained all 495 original rows across 67 tables, then passed native sign-in, role-filtered reads, saved-output comparison, writes and repeated setup.
Local people sign in again because Base now scopes local cookies to their origin; their native session records are retained.
Restore preserves planning memberships and historical attribution, but excludes native identities, sessions and credentials.
The destination keeps its own owner; membership alone cannot sign anyone in.
Live `actorNames` projections resolve only names available in the destination's native directory, while names stored inside immutable snapshots remain unchanged (subject to `ERASE-001`).
A pre-upgrade export restores only with the release that made it.
Keep a private export and that release before upgrading.

To recover, restore into an empty installation of that release, upgrade that installation in place by running `rer install` and `rer setup` inside that existing checkout, then export again with the upgraded release.
Do not import a pre-upgrade export directly into a newer release.

Finance alone creates, revises, disables and reads cash alert rules and reads and acknowledges their alerts.
Every rule checks the operating forecast in the reporting currency, in integer cents.

*Forecast cash below the floor* uses the `FIN-005` agreed floor: it breaches when any month after the latest closed month closes strictly below the floor (equality meets it), and names that crossing month and the lowest forecast month and amount.

*Actual cash below plan* compares the latest closed month's closing cash in the forecast, which is on accepted actuals (ledger figures, not bank balances), with the approved budget's closing cash for that month; it breaches when the shortfall is strictly more than the rule's amount, or strictly more than its percent of a positive plan (a nonpositive plan has no percentage and is reported as not assessed).
*Runway below N months* uses `FIN-005`'s exact unrounded ratio at the earliest month after the latest closed month; non-burning positive cash never breaches.

Rules are checked after every accepted or undone actuals file, every month close, every cash-floor or rule save and finance's explicit check, and once a day at 08:00 in the saved company zone (daylight saving included); each scheduled check is recorded with its zone and its scheduled and actual times, and the scheduled run acts as `scheduler:cash-alerts` for the still-active owner or admin who last saved an enabled rule.

A check that finds no breach ends the alert without a message, and revising or disabling a rule ends its open alert, so the next breach opens a new one.
Acknowledgment records the finance person and time against the latest send, once per send, and does not change when the alert sends again.

An entity plans in its local currency and reports in USD, using rate tables that finance keeps (budget rate, monthly average and month-end rates).

This installation's plan is the entity: its plan currency is the local currency, and finance names one reporting currency (USD by default; never the plan currency).

Finance keeps one rate row per month with a budget, an average and a month-end rate, each the reporting-currency amount of one unit of plan currency, a decimal above zero with at most six places, stored as integer millionths.
Rates are read when a view is built, so revising a rate changes every scenario view (working or frozen) but never rewrites a stored calculation, approved budget, kept forecast or published pack.
Every amount is translated once from the plan's own integer cents, rounding half away from zero, and totals are sums of translated parts, so each statement foots.
Profit and loss translates each month at that month's average rate.

The balance sheet translates every line at the month-end rate; opening equity at the month-end rate of the month before the plan; retained earnings as the running sum of translated monthly profit; contributed equity as the running sum of each month's change at that month's average rate.

The translation adjustment is translated assets minus liabilities minus equity, less the plan's own balance difference (which is translated and carried visibly, never absorbed), shown as a running balance and as the month's movement.

A month lacking the rate it needs (average for profit, month-end for the balance sheet, the month-end before the plan for opening equity, or an earlier average for the running sums) is listed as unavailable with the missing rate and is never zero or guessed.
Cash-flow statements are not translated.

For a closed month the constant-currency variance translates the approved budget at the budget rate and actual at the average rate and again at the budget rate: variance = actual − budget, constant-currency variance = actual at the budget rate − budget, and currency effect = actual − actual at the budget rate, so variance = constant-currency variance + currency effect; totals are profit (revenue minus costs) from rounded rows.
A reader sees translated amounts only from the same scenario and variance views their role already reads; only finance edits rates, and the rate table is in the open export.

Each kept forecast is compared with the months that closed after it, by line, department, driver sources and month, carrying confirmed explanations.

The error (actual minus kept) is split exactly: timing is twice the amount that offsets itself across the closed months for one line and department; driver is the part of the remaining net error that the measured revisions below would have removed; permanent is the rest.

Three assumptions are measured: close-date slippage (mean whole days, half away from zero, from deal history), hire slippage (mean days between planned and actual start in accepted roster history) and collection lag (observed days from invoice to payment less the linked contract's planned DSO).

A measure needs at least three observations, a non-zero mean and at least six kept forecasts that still recalculate to their stored cells; a backtest uses the last up to twelve, revises only inputs that had not started when the forecast was kept, and compares summed absolute error against what actually closed (collection lag compares monthly collections of the linked invoices).
A suggestion is made only when the revision lowers that error.

`learning-propose` creates a draft proposal from the current forecast that cites the backtest and moves only inputs that have not started; the forecast, kept forecasts and snapshots change only when finance submits and promotes that exact proposal revision through the ordinary doors.

Easel is a US-first FP&A product. These are the jobs it deliberately does not do, and how a buyer gets each one done.

**The ledger and the close.** Easel is not the accounting system of record and never posts journals. Bookkeeping, the close, reconciliations and audited GAAP statements stay in [Pantry](https://github.com/just-every/run-pantry), QuickBooks Online, Xero, NetSuite or Sage Intacct, which Easel reads (`CONNECT-*`). Close-management tools such as FloQast and BlackLine stay separate.

**Payroll and tax filing.** Easel estimates employer cost and taxes for planning (`FIN-006`, `PEOPLE-004`). It never runs payroll or files Form 941, Form 940, W-2 or 1099. That stays with Gusto, Rippling, ADP RUN or the buyer's PEO; the RunEditRun payroll sibling is [Envelope](https://github.com/just-every/run-envelope). Income-tax figures are planning estimates; filings and tax advice come from the buyer's CPA (whose practice may run on [Blotter](https://github.com/just-every/run-blotter)).

**Treasury and payments.** Easel recommends; it does not move money. Payments, transfers, credit-line draws and collections run in the bank, Bill.com or the ledger. Bank access through Plaid is read-only (`CONNECT-009`).

**CRM, HRIS, ATS, billing, expenses and procurement.** These belong to [Orbit](https://github.com/just-every/run-orbit), [Willow](https://github.com/just-every/run-willow), [Lodge](https://github.com/just-every/run-lodge), [Nectar](https://github.com/just-every/run-nectar), [Coaster](https://github.com/just-every/run-coaster) and [Purse](https://github.com/just-every/run-purse), or their US incumbents. Easel reads them and never writes deals, employees, offers, invoices or purchase orders.

**A full spreadsheet engine.** Easel does not re-implement every Excel function or VBA. Excel and Google Sheets stay the buyer's spreadsheets, connected live (`SHEET-001`, `SHEET-002`). Formulas Easel cannot translate are listed and kept as values with provenance (`SHEET-003`).

**Statutory consolidation and disclosure.** Easel does management consolidation for a few entities (`ENTITY-001`). Statutory consolidation, minority interests, SEC reporting and audit-ready disclosure belong in the ledger or a specialist consolidation tool.

**Warehouse-scale analytics.** Large event data is processed in Snowflake, BigQuery or Databricks and arrives as metrics (`REPORT-007`). Easel's models stay within `MODEL-007`'s scale, with larger work run as bounded background jobs.
**Hosting frontier models.** Agents call the owner's chosen model provider under the owner's budget (`AGENT-011`). Easel hosts no model.
**Native app distribution.** This needs Apple and Google developer accounts. That is release engineering (`MOBILE-002`), not a reason to drop the apps.

**Region, currency and language.** US-first: USD by default, US English, US payroll and tax assumptions and the buyer's own Cloudflare account. Other currencies are planned through `ENTITY-002`. Localized interfaces and non-US payroll rules are not claimed.
